data.summary: The pod startup exceeded the 10.0-second SLO, taking 21.0 seconds to become Ready. This was primarily due to a slow image pull, which took 19.391 seconds for a 53 MB image. The observed throughput of 2.8 MB/s was well below the typical 5 MB/s threshold, indicating a bottleneck with the registry or network.

findings.statement: The total pod startup time was 21.0 seconds, exceeding the SLO threshold of 10.0 seconds.
The image_pull phase was the longest phase, lasting 19.391 seconds.
The image size was 53,328,919 bytes (approximately 53 MB).
The image pull throughput was 2,750,189 bytes/s (2.8 MB/s), which is below the typical 5 MB/s threshold for a healthy registry.

ruled_out.reason: The image size of 53 MB is not considered large enough to be the primary cause when throughput is significantly degraded, as indicated by the slow_registry runbook.
The model loading time (model_s) was 0.0 seconds.
The app_init phase took 0.952 seconds, which is a small fraction of the total startup time.
The scheduling phase took 0.0 seconds, and there were no failed scheduling events.
The readiness phase took 0.0 seconds, and there were no probe failures after the app was ready.

recommendations.rationale: Pre-pulling the image can prevent scale-up from being dependent on real-time registry throughput.

recommendations.action: Advisory: use a registry mirror or pull-through cache close to the cluster; check registry rate limits.
recommendations.rationale: Improving the network path to the registry or mitigating rate limits can increase image pull throughput.
